back: The gradual, orderly change of a plant community through time as each stage modifies the habitat and is replaced by the next.
Sere: the whole sequence of communities to the climax. Seral stage: one community in the sequence.
Crustose lichens, mosses and foliose lichens, annual herbs and ferns, perennial grasses, shrubs, trees (climax).
Open water, submerged and floating plants, reedswamp, marsh or sedge meadow, shrubs, woodland.
Primary starts with no soil (rock, water) and is slow. Secondary starts with soil after fire, felling or abandonment and is faster.
Hardy species that colonise bare or disturbed ground first and prepare the habitat for later species.
The relatively stable final community, in balance with climate and soil.
A community held at an earlier stage than the climatic climax by human activity such as burning or grazing.
Species diversity, biomass, soil depth, organic matter and food web complexity increase.
